task: HM-S12-01: deterministic simulation of the HiveMind compute market (Kelly consumers, Tullock workers, multi-queue routing)

hypotheses.H-M1: every Kelly equilibrium over random linear valuations (2-12 consumers, values log-uniform in [0.1, 100]) has efficiency >= 0.75 (Johari-Tsitsiklis bound) and feasible shares (sum 1, all >= 0)
hypotheses.H-M2: every closed-form Tullock equilibrium (2-8 workers, costs log-uniform in [0.1, 10], pool log-uniform in [1, 1000]) passes the epsilon-Nash grid certificate at eps = 1e-6 of the pool; the equilibrium price per cobblestone exceeds the cheapest cost (rents exist)
hypotheses.H-M3: best-response routing over 2-6 workers and 1-4 queues converges in <= 500 rounds and is epsilon-Nash (1e-6) in >= 95% of instances; when no worker is capacity-bound the queue prices equalise

controls.positive: 1 consumer of value 1 vs 50 of value 1/2 must give efficiency in [0.75, 0.77] (the bound is approached: the metric measures the game)
controls.negative: three symmetric workers split a pool exactly evenly; two equal consumers split capacity 1/2-1/2

decision_rule: simulation valid iff both controls pass; the market design is 'proposed' (not 'adopted') until the live-ledger integration HM-S12-02 reproduces H-M1/H-M2 on real receipts
not_measured: strategic misreporting of FLOPs (handled by verified_credit, not by the market)
